blocks.markdown: Spanish doesn't have a normal verb "to like" — instead, **gustar** literally means "to be pleasing to", and the grammatical subject is the *thing liked*, not the person. **Me gusta el café** literally means "Coffee is pleasing to me", even though it translates as "I like coffee". The pronoun in front (**me**, **te**, **le**, **nos**, **os**, **les**) marks *who* is doing the liking.

The verb itself only ever agrees with the *thing liked*: **gusta** for one thing (*Me gusta el café*), **gustan** for more than one (*Me gustan las manzanas* — "Apples are pleasing to me"/"I like apples").

exercises.prompt: ___ gusta el café. (me — I like coffee.)
¿Te ___ el vino? (gustar — Do you like wine? — singular thing liked)
Translate: "I like apples." (plural thing liked — gustan)
